unrelatedProcesses.note: The channel is created for a direct child.

localEndpoint.note: Platform pipe is not exposed as a general server endpoint.

encryptedTransport.note: No transport authentication or encryption API.

broadcastPubSub.note: Requires application fan-out to child channels.

automaticReconnect.note: Process and channel restart are application-owned.

queueingBackpressure.note: send() reports channel backlog, but the application owns throttling and queue limits.

crossLanguage.note: The documented message API targets Node child processes.

handlePassing.note: sendHandle supports selected socket/server handles with platform limits.

parentChild.note: A parent and child must create or connect to an explicit TCP or local endpoint; net does not create a dedicated channel.

unrelatedProcesses.note: TCP and IPC servers accept independent clients.

tcp.note: TCP client and server APIs are built in.

localEndpoint.note: Unix sockets and Windows named pipes are documented.

udp.note: Datagrams use node:dgram rather than node:net.

encryptedTransport.note: TLS uses node:tls over a stream.

namedEvents.note: Framing and event dispatch are application-owned.

broadcastPubSub.note: Applications track and fan out to sockets.

automaticReconnect.note: Reconnect and retry policy are application-owned.

queueingBackpressure.note: write() and drain expose stream backpressure; queue limits and policy remain application-owned.

browserClient.note: Raw TCP/local sockets are unavailable to browser JavaScript.

crossLanguage.note: Peers can implement an application-defined stream protocol.

handlePassing.note: Handle passing is provided by child_process, not net alone.

parentChild.note: The same client/server API works between related processes.

unrelatedProcesses.note: Local and network servers accept independent clients.

tcp.note: TCP client and server transports are built in.

localEndpoint.note: Unix sockets and Windows named pipes are built in.

udp.note: UDP4 and UDP6 server/client modes are built in.

encryptedTransport.note: TLS and Assured mutual TLS are configurable product capabilities; the benchmark Fast profile did not exercise encryption.

namedEvents.note: Event names are part of the public API.

automaticReconnect.note: Stream clients have configurable retry intervals, retry limits, and a stop switch.

queueingBackpressure.note: Guarded and Assured bound pending stream bytes; the benchmark Fast profile writes directly. Sync mode can serialize requests.

browserClient.note: The package targets Node-style socket transports.

crossLanguage.note: Documented Node and Rust implementations share the protocol.

parentChild.note: WebSocket works between any reachable peers.

unrelatedProcesses.note: Client and server can run independently.

localEndpoint.note: The documented ws+unix form supports IPC endpoints.

broadcastPubSub.note: The documented broadcast pattern loops over clients.

queueingBackpressure.note: bufferedAmount and send callbacks expose queue state, but applications own limits and policy.

browserClient.note: Browsers provide a native WebSocket client.

parentChild.note: Socket.IO works between any reachable client and server.

unrelatedProcesses.note: Clients and servers are independently addressable.

tcp.note: HTTP long-polling and WebSocket provide TCP/IP lanes; WebTransport is also documented.

localEndpoint.note: Not claimed as a portable first-class endpoint in the cited docs.

udp.note: Socket.IO exposes no raw UDP datagram API; WebTransport is not a raw UDP lane.

encryptedTransport.note: An HTTPS server supplies authenticated encryption when certificates and trust are configured.

namedEvents.note: Named events are the primary API.

broadcastPubSub.note: Broadcasting and rooms are built in.

automaticReconnect.note: The client exposes configurable reconnection, delay, and attempt settings.

queueingBackpressure.note: The client buffers events while disconnected; this is in-memory buffering, not durable or exactly-once delivery.

browserClient.note: The official client package targets browsers and Node.js.

crossLanguage.note: The documented Socket.IO protocol has implementations in multiple languages.

handlePassing.note: No handle-transfer API is exposed by the documented protocol.

parentChild.note: Sockets work between any reachable peers; no parent-child-only channel is created.

unrelatedProcesses.note: Message sockets bind and connect independently.

tcp.note: TCP is a standard ZeroMQ transport.

localEndpoint.note: ipc:// depends on Unix-domain sockets and is not a Windows named-pipe transport.

udp.note: UDP is an experimental draft transport limited to Radio/Dish sockets.

encryptedTransport.note: CURVE authentication and encryption are available when configured; CURVE is not TLS.

namedEvents.note: Topics and socket patterns exist, but application event envelopes are manual.

requestReply.note: REQ/REP and DEALER/ROUTER patterns are built in.

automaticReconnect.note: Connection-oriented sockets expose reconnect interval controls.

queueingBackpressure.note: High-water marks bound in-memory queues; behavior can block or drop by socket type and is not durable delivery.

browserClient.note: The default package is a native Node addon, not a browser client.

crossLanguage.note: ZMTP is a documented wire protocol with implementations across languages.

handlePassing.note: No Node handle-transfer API is exposed.
